arbitrum.identity: Offchain Labs, Inc., the developer of the Arbitrum Ethereum layer-2 (founders Ed Felten, Steven Goldfeder, Harry Kalodner)
arbitrum.note: Ribbit is named in Offchain Labs' Series B led by Lightspeed (Aug 2021, $1.2B valuation per the release headline); the earlier $20M Series A investors were undisclosed, so entry is Growth. The band uses ARB's circulating market cap today ($1.36B, FDV $2.0B) as the listed instrument for protocol rows, which agrees with the $1.2B equity round; HQ is from the release's New York dateline (the company was founded in Princeton).

cowboy-space.identity: Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux Inc.), orbital AI data centers, satellites and launch vehicle, founded 2024 by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt
cowboy-space.note: The $275M Series B led by Index Ventures valued it at $2B (May 2026); Ribbit is not named among the Series A (Apr 2025, Index and Interlagos) or Series B investors and appears only on Ribbit's own portfolio page, so the round Ribbit joined is undetermined. Focus read as space hardware (rockets, satellites); Climate & Energy is the alternative given its space-solar origin.

deel.identity: Deel, Inc., global payroll and HR platform (founders Alex Bouaziz, Shuo Wang)
deel.note: Ribbit co-led the $300M Series E with Andreessen Horowitz at a $17.3B valuation in Oct 2025, and no earlier Deel round names Ribbit. Payroll and HR software read as SaaS; HQ San Francisco per its LinkedIn company page (incorporated in Delaware, remote-first).

enter.identity: Enter, São Paulo legal AI company (founders Mateus Costa-Ribeiro, Michael Mac-Vicar, Henrique Vaz)
enter.note: Ribbit is first named in the $100M+ Series B led by Founders Fund at $1.2B (May 2026); the $35M Series A of Sept 2025 named only Founders Fund and Sequoia as co-leads. Enter sells AI agents that run enterprise litigation, so AI & Applied AI.

parafin.identity: Parafin, Inc., embedded small-business financing (founders Sahil Phadnis, Vineet Goel, Ralph Furman)
parafin.note: Parafin's own Series B post names Thrive and Ribbit as the leads of its seed and Series A, which were announced together in Sept 2021 ($34M), so entry is Seed (the seed's own close month is undisclosed). The latest priced figure is $750M at the Dec 2024 Series C; the 2026 blog items are credit and forward-flow facilities, not equity.

privy.identity: Privy (Horkos, Inc.), New York embedded crypto wallet infrastructure (founders Henri Stern, Asta Li)
privy.note: Ribbit led an unnamed $15M round in Mar 2025 that followed the 2022 seed (Sequoia, BlueYard) and the 2023 $18M Series A (Paradigm), so it is read as a post-A round, Growth. Stripe acquired Privy in June 2025 for an undisclosed sum (Stripe's Wikipedia page), so acquired and below_1b.

relay-payments.identity: Relay Payments, Atlanta trucking and logistics payments company (founders Ryan Droege, Spencer Barkoff)
relay-payments.note: The Jan 2021 announcement says Addition led the Series A ($7.7M, Jul 2020) and Series B ($35.3M, Dec 2020) 'with participation from' Ribbit and Spark, read as Ribbit in both rounds, though the sentence does not split investors by round (Growth if Ribbit joined only the B). No priced figure of $1B or more found; its 2026 newsroom shows it still operating.

solana.identity: Solana Labs, Inc., the San Francisco developer of the Solana blockchain (founders Anatoly Yakovenko, Raj Gokal)
solana.note: No priced Solana Labs equity round naming Ribbit was found (Wikipedia's account of the June 2021 $314M SOL sale led by a16z and Polychain does not name Ribbit), so the position reads as tokens and entry is undetermined. Solana Labs has no priced equity figure, so the band uses SOL's circulating market cap today ($69.2B, FDV $74.8B) as the listed instrument, the same rule as Arbitrum.

teya.identity: Teya (formerly SaltPay), London payments and software provider for European small businesses (founders Thiago Piau, Ali Mazanderani, Eduardo Pontes)
teya.note: SaltPay raised over $1B (Nilson Report) and vendors show $2.4B for a Nov 2021 round, but no reputable outlet published a priced figure that I could fetch, so Rule A gives below_1b despite the likely unicorn value. Only a vendor database (multiples.vc) places Ribbit in a Jan 2020 Series A led by LTS Investments, with no press confirmation, so entry is undetermined.
